question.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ of three nails is drawn from a population. The population has nails of two different lengths, $5\,\text{cm}$ and $\text{10}\,\text{cm},$ distributed in the ratio $4:1.$ Calculate the standard error of $\overset{―}{X}.$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We're told that the nails in the population have lengths $5\,\text{cm}$ and $\text{10}\,\text{cm},$ and these are distributed in the ratio $4:1.$ Therefore, to compute the population mean and variance, we can consider a population consisting of $4+1=5$ nails only with the following lengths:

$$
5\,\text{cm},\,5\,\text{cm},\,5\,\text{cm},\,5\,\text{cm}\,10\,\text{cm}.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(4\cdot 5+10) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(20+10) \\  & =\frac{30}{5} \\  & =6\,\text{cm},\end{aligned}
$$

and the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}^{2}-{\mu }^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(4\cdot {5}^{2}+{10}^{2})-{6}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(200)-36 \\  & =40-36 \\  & =4\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the sample size $n=3,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}=\frac{4}{3}\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.
$$

Finally,

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\frac{4}{3}}≈1.15\,\text{cm}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
